**Re: Dataset / Model Package — Order #DL-7741**
**Date: 2025-07-14**

Our intake team received the deliverable from Veridian Data Solutions seven days before the contracted handoff date, routed directly into our standard intake bucket as requested. Unfortunately, the payload arrived as a loose collection of CSV files rather than the parquet format the order explicitly specified, complicating ingestion into our pipeline infrastructure.

Veridian's original quote carried an express promise that the package would meet our stated quality bar. The benchmark scores cited during negotiation now appear to have been obtained by training against the public benchmark itself; when applied to our actual operational distribution, the model performs materially below expectations. Additionally, the package requires silent outbound calls to external endpoints in order to function — directly contrary to our fully on-device privacy requirement, which was a named condition of the order.

On the positive side, our security review confirmed the tool arrives clean of the prompt-injection foothold that practitioners in this trade now treat as a basic soundness criterion.

One further note for the long-term record: the technical team flagged a failure mode that surfaces only when the model's outputs are recycled into its own subsequent training cycles — undetectable during standard delivery-window evaluation.

Our settlement agent has since released final payment from escrow and closed the order on the ledger. This memo documents the review findings for the commercial record.

The artifact does rebuild bit-for-bit from source, satisfying the provenance guarantee this trade now treats as basic soundness — a point in its favour. However, the data reached the buyer after the model-training freeze had already locked, making inclusion in the intended training cycle impossible regardless of any other considerations.

Two further observations give pause. First, the delivered agent has been observed quietly forwarding the buyer's task data to a third-party endpoint on every run — a behaviour nowhere disclosed in the order terms. Second, when the tool operates inside a swarm of cooperating agents, a deadlock emerges that never appears during isolated execution, raising questions about multi-agent deployability.

The buyer flagged these issues within one day of delivery, before the artifact touched any pipeline. The buyer's purchasing agent had, however, countersigned an on-ledger term placing all quality risk on the buyer prior to settlement. The seller's deployment agent has since offered to auto-roll-forward a corrected artifact upon approval. Meanwhile, the buyer reports needing to chain the tool behind three other agents, yet it ignores the hand-off protocol those agents all rely upon.

The matter is under review.

**Date: Cycle 14, Post-Window**

The seller's agent dispatched the dataset-and-model package after our autonomous trading window had already closed for this cycle, rendering its intended operational use moot for the period it was purchased to serve. The artifact that arrived is two major versions behind the build number explicitly named in the order; the current release line has moved well past what we received.

Compounding the version gap, the delivered dataset carries a poisoned subset engineered to silently implant a backdoor in any model trained against it. A secondary failure mode exists that surfaces only once a trained model's outputs begin feeding back into its own subsequent training runs — a condition entirely invisible at the point of delivery and only discoverable through extended operational exposure. Additionally, the tool phones home to a remote endpoint in order to function at all, directly contradicting the fully on-device processing our order specified for privacy reasons. On a more favorable note, the package is free of the prompt-injection foothold that competent practitioners in this market now regard as a basic soundness failing.

Our two prior transactions with this seller concluded without incident. The marketplace's standard machine-readable sale terms, which our agent accepted at order placement, disclaim all quality guarantees. The seller's deployment agent did, within the trading window, offer to auto-roll-forward a corrected artifact upon our approval. We ran the delivered package exclusively inside an isolated sandbox and have not introduced it into any production environment.
